QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_8

question.text: Which of the following is categorised under 'Investor-level risks' rather than 'Fund-level (governance) risks' in Chapter 7 of the workbook?

answer.text: Lack of transparency and unethical practices in fund governance.
Sub-optimal structuring of investment contracts with investee companies by the manager.
Risk of adverse selection of the fund manager at the time of PPM subscription.
Macroeconomic changes such as currency depreciation affecting foreign LP repatriation.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 134-136), investor-level risks include the risk of adverse selection in choosing the right fund manager, illiquidity and uncertainty, fund-monitoring difficulty, cash management for capital calls, underlying investment risks and debt financing risks. Governance/fiduciary risks, fund-management (sub-optimal contracting) risks and macroeconomic risks are categorised separately as fund-structure, fund-management or macro-level fund risks. The Trap: Options A, B and D map to the three non-investor categories listed in the chapter: governance/fiduciary, fund management, and macroeconomic. Adverse selection at the PPM-evaluation stage is uniquely investor-side because the LP must choose among managers before any fund exists. Note: The investor-level vs fund-level taxonomy is set out on pages 134-136; the three distractor categories are all explicitly named in the chapter.
